title: 2 Kings Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who came to Hezekiah when he was sick unto death?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah the son of Amoz
questions.explanation: Isaiah the son of Amoz came to Hezekiah when he was sick unto death as stated in 2 Kings 20:1.

questions.question: What did the LORD tell Hezekiah through Isaiah regarding his condition?
options: Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die
Go to the temple and fast
questions.correctAnswer: Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die
questions.explanation: The LORD told Hezekiah through Isaiah to set his house in order because he would die, as said in 2 Kings 20:1.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do after hearing the prophet's message?
options: Turned his face to the wall and prayed
Called the priests to pray for him
questions.correctAnswer: Turned his face to the wall and prayed
questions.explanation: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed unto the LORD after hearing the message, as recorded in 2 Kings 20:2.

questions.question: In his prayer, how did Hezekiah describe the way he had walked before the LORD?
options: In truth and with a perfect heart
questions.correctAnswer: In truth and with a perfect heart
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed that he had walked before the LORD in truth and with a perfect heart, as in 2 Kings 20:3.

questions.question: What was Hezekiah's emotional response when he prayed to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: He wept sore
questions.explanation: The text states that Hezekiah wept sore after his prayer in 2 Kings 20:3.

questions.question: Before Isaiah had gone out into the middle court, what happened?
options: The word of the LORD came to Isaiah
The king of Assyria sent a message
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came to Isaiah
questions.explanation: Before Isaiah had gone out into the middle court, the word of the LORD came to him as described in 2 Kings 20:4.

questions.question: What did God promise Hezekiah through Isaiah after hearing his prayer and seeing his tears?
options: He would heal him and he would go up to the house of the LORD on the third day
He would be taken captive by Assyria
He would become king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He would heal him and he would go up to the house of the LORD on the third day
questions.explanation: God promised through Isaiah that Hezekiah would be healed and would go up to the house of the LORD on the third day as in 2 Kings 20:5.

questions.question: How many years did God add to Hezekiah's life?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteen years
questions.explanation: God said He would add fifteen years to Hezekiah's life as recorded in 2 Kings 20:6.

questions.question: What did God promise to do for Jerusalem during Hezekiah's extended life?
options: Deliver the city from the king of Assyria and defend it
Make the city a trading center
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver the city from the king of Assyria and defend it
questions.explanation: God promised to deliver Jerusalem out of the hand of the king of Assyria and defend it for His own sake and for David's sake as in 2 Kings 20:6.

questions.question: What remedy did Isaiah give to Hezekiah to help him recover?
options: Take a lump of figs and lay it on the boil
questions.correctAnswer: Take a lump of figs and lay it on the boil
questions.explanation: Isaiah instructed to take a lump of figs and lay it on the boil to help Hezekiah recover as in 2 Kings 20:7.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah asked Isaiah what sign would prove that the LORD would heal him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hezekiah asked Isaiah what sign would show that the LORD would heal him, as recorded in 2 Kings 20:8.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah asked Hezekiah if the shadow on the dial should go forward or backward ten degrees as a sign.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah asked Hezekiah if the shadow should go forward or backward ten degrees as a sign, as stated in 2 Kings 20:9.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah said it was easier for the shadow to go forward ten degrees than backward.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hezekiah said it was a light thing for the shadow to go down (forward) ten degrees, but he requested it to go backward ten degrees, as in 2 Kings 20:10.

questions.question: True or False: The shadow moved backward ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz as a sign from the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah prayed and the shadow moved backward ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz, confirming the sign, as narrated in 2 Kings 20:11.

questions.question: In what order do these events happen in 2 Kings 20: First Hezekiah prays, second Isaiah receives the word of the LORD, third God promises to add years to Hezekiah's life, fourth the shadow moves backward. Which event comes first?
options: Isaiah receives the word of the LORD
God promises to add years to Hezekiah's life
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah prays
questions.explanation: Hezekiah first turned to pray (verse 2), then Isaiah received the word of the LORD (verse 4), followed by God's promise (verse 6), and finally the shadow moved backward (verse 11).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What sign did Isaiah give Hezekiah to confirm that the LORD would heal him?
options: The shadow on the dial of Ahaz would go backward ten degrees
A rainbow would appear in the sky
He would dream a special dream
questions.correctAnswer: The shadow on the dial of Ahaz would go backward ten degrees
questions.explanation: Isaiah told Hezekiah that God would confirm His promise by making the shadow go backward ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz, as recorded in 2 Kings 20:9-11.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah respond to the choice between the shadow moving forward or backward?
options: He chose the shadow to return backward ten degrees
He chose the shadow to move forward ten degrees
He asked for a different sign
questions.correctAnswer: He chose the shadow to return backward ten degrees
questions.explanation: Hezekiah said it would be a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees, but he preferred the shadow to return backward ten degrees, as described in 2 Kings 20:10.

questions.question: What was Berodachbaladan's reason for sending letters and a present to Hezekiah?
options: Because he had heard Hezekiah was sick
To form an alliance against Assyria
To congratulate Hezekiah on his victories
questions.correctAnswer: Because he had heard Hezekiah was sick
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:12 states that Berodachbaladan sent letters and a present because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah respond to the envoys from Babylon?
options: He showed them all his treasures and precious things
He refused to meet with them
He sent them away without answering
He asked them to leave a gift and depart
questions.correctAnswer: He showed them all his treasures and precious things
questions.explanation: Hezekiah listened to the envoys and showed them all his treasures, as described in 2 Kings 20:13.

questions.question: What did Isaiah ask Hezekiah concerning the men from Babylon?
options: What they said and from where they came
If Hezekiah planned to ally with Babylon
If Hezekiah had accepted their gifts
questions.correctAnswer: What they said and from where they came
questions.explanation: Isaiah inquired what the men said and from where they had come, according to 2 Kings 20:14.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah admit to Isaiah about what the Babylonian envoys had seen?
options: They had seen all the treasures in his house
They only saw the outer court
They were not allowed inside the palace
They saw only the silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: They had seen all the treasures in his house
questions.explanation: Hezekiah told Isaiah that the envoys saw all the treasures in his house, as stated in 2 Kings 20:15.

questions.question: What did Isaiah prophesy would happen to the treasures of Hezekiah's house?
options: They would be carried away into Babylon
They would be hidden and preserved
They would be given as gifts to Egypt
They would be destroyed in a fire
questions.correctAnswer: They would be carried away into Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah declared that the treasures and those stored by his fathers would be carried into Babylon, as written in 2 Kings 20:17.

questions.question: According to Isaiah, what would happen to Hezekiah's sons?
options: They would be taken and made eunuchs in Babylon
They would become kings of Judah
They would lead a rebellion against Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: They would be taken and made eunuchs in Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah foretold that Hezekiah’s sons would be taken away and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon, as in 2 Kings 20:18.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah react to the prophecy Isaiah spoke about the future captivity?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hezekiah said that the word of the LORD spoken by Isaiah was good, showing acceptance of the prophecy, according to 2 Kings 20:19.

questions.question: Did Hezekiah build a pool and conduit to bring water into the city according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The chapter mentions Hezekiah’s acts of making a pool and conduit to bring water into the city in 2 Kings 20:20.

questions.question: Was Hezekiah’s healing immediate without any sign from God?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God provided a sign through the miraculous shadow moving backward to confirm Hezekiah’s healing, as shown in 2 Kings 20:9-11.

questions.question: What lesson about prayer and faith can be learned from Hezekiah’s experience in this chapter?
options: Faith and prayer can lead to God extending life and granting healing
Prayer has no effect on God’s plans
Only prophets can intercede for healing
Healing requires no faith or prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and prayer can lead to God extending life and granting healing
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s prayer and faith led God to grant him fifteen more years of life and healing, as seen in 2 Kings 20:1-6.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 20:17 promise will happen if the reader does what 2 Kings 20:13 describes Hezekiah doing?
options: The treasures shown to outsiders will eventually be taken away into Babylon
The treasures will be protected forever
The treasures will multiply and increase
The treasures will be hidden and preserved
questions.correctAnswer: The treasures shown to outsiders will eventually be taken away into Babylon
questions.explanation: Hezekiah showed all his treasures to the Babylonian envoys in 2 Kings 20:13, and Isaiah later prophesied in 2 Kings 20:17 that all those treasures would be taken into Babylon as a consequence.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is illustrated by Hezekiah turning to the LORD in prayer when he was sick?
options: Ignoring God in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and dependence on God
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s turning to prayer and pleading with God in humility during his illness demonstrates the virtue of depending on God, as shown in 2 Kings 20:2-3.

questions.question: Based on 2 Kings 20, what biblical truth applies to a believer who is tempted to show off their blessings to others?
options: Revealing all your blessings can lead to future loss or hardship
It is wise to flaunt blessings to gain favor
Blessings should always be hidden from others
God rewards those who boast about their wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Revealing all your blessings can lead to future loss or hardship
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s openness with the Babylonian envoys about his treasures led Isaiah to prophesy their eventual captivity and loss, teaching a caution about revealing all blessings, as seen in 2 Kings 20:13-18.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 20.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah show to the messengers from Babylon?
options: All the treasures in his house and dominion
Only the gold and silver in his treasury
Nothing, he refused to show them anything
questions.correctAnswer: All the treasures in his house and dominion
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:13 states that Hezekiah showed the Babylonian messengers all the precious things in his house, including silver, gold, spices, ointment, armour, and all treasures.

questions.question: Who was Berodachbaladan, as mentioned in 2 Kings 20?
questions.correctAnswer: King of Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:12 identifies Berodachbaladan as the son of Baladan and king of Babylon who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah.

questions.question: What prophecy did Isaiah deliver to Hezekiah concerning his descendants?
options: They will be taken captive to Babylon and become eunuchs
They will reign forever in Jerusalem
They will build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: They will be taken captive to Babylon and become eunuchs
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:18 states that Isaiah prophesied that some of Hezekiah's sons would be taken away to Babylon and made eunuchs in the king's palace.

questions.question: What is the significance of Hezekiah's response to Isaiah's prophecy in 2 Kings 20:19?
options: He accepted the word of the LORD as good, valuing peace and truth in his days
He sought to rebel against Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He accepted the word of the LORD as good, valuing peace and truth in his days
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:19 records Hezekiah saying the word of the LORD is good because it promises peace and truth during his lifetime.

questions.question: What engineering works of Hezekiah are mentioned in 2 Kings 20:20?
options: A pool and a conduit to bring water into the city
questions.correctAnswer: A pool and a conduit to bring water into the city
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:20 mentions Hezekiah's construction of a pool and conduit to bring water into Jerusalem, highlighting his practical measures for the city's defense and sustenance.

questions.question: To whom did the kingship pass after Hezekiah’s death?
questions.correctAnswer: Manasseh, his son
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:21 states that after Hezekiah died, his son Manasseh reigned in his place.

questions.question: The prophecy that treasures of Hezekiah and his fathers would be carried into Babylon is an example of what theme often found in the Old Testament?
questions.correctAnswer: Exile and captivity as judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:17's prophecy of treasures being taken to Babylon reflects the Old Testament theme of exile and captivity as consequences of disobedience to God (cf. Jeremiah 25:11-12).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a prophecy about the Babylonian exile that complements the warning in 2 Kings 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah contains detailed prophecies about the Babylonian exile that complement Isaiah's warnings to Hezekiah in 2 Kings 20:17-18.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'eunuchs' in 2 Kings 20:18 carries a significant cultural meaning in the ancient Near East?
options: Saris, meaning palace officials often castrated to serve kings
questions.correctAnswer: Saris, meaning palace officials often castrated to serve kings
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'saris' (translated eunuchs) in 2 Kings 20:18 refers to castrated males who served in royal courts, a common practice in the ancient Near East to ensure loyalty and prevent lineage threats.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God extending life in response to prayer, similar to Hezekiah’s healing in 2 Kings 20?
questions.correctAnswer: James 5:14-15
questions.explanation: James 5:14-15 speaks of prayer for the sick leading to healing, echoing the theme of God responding to Hezekiah’s prayer for life extension in 2 Kings 20.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the shadow moving backward on the dial of Ahaz as a sign to Hezekiah?
options: Miraculous sign as a divine confirmation
questions.correctAnswer: Miraculous sign as a divine confirmation
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:11 describes the shadow moving backward as a miraculous sign from God to confirm the prophecy of healing, a common literary device in biblical narratives to authenticate divine messages.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah’s prayer to the LORD included a plea to remember how he walked before God in truth and with a perfect heart.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:3 records Hezekiah praying to the LORD, asking Him to remember how he had walked before Him in truth and with a perfect heart.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah immediately left the palace without delivering any message to Hezekiah after his prayer.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:4-5 shows that before Isaiah left the palace, the word of the LORD came to him instructing him to tell Hezekiah he would be healed and granted fifteen more years of life.

questions.question: What does the episode of Hezekiah showing all his treasures to the Babylonian envoys foreshadow in biblical history?
options: The eventual Babylonian conquest and exile
questions.correctAnswer: The eventual Babylonian conquest and exile
questions.explanation: Hezekiah’s revealing of treasures to Babylonian envoys (2 Kings 20:13) foreshadows the future Babylonian conquest and exile prophesied in verses 17-18.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 20 illustrate the theme of divine mercy despite impending judgment?
options: God extends Hezekiah’s life but warns of future exile
God promises no judgment at all
questions.correctAnswer: God extends Hezekiah’s life but warns of future exile
questions.explanation: The chapter shows God’s mercy in granting Hezekiah 15 more years (2 Kings 20:6) while also warning through Isaiah about future Babylonian exile (2 Kings 20:17), blending mercy with judgment.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's response to Hezekiah's prayer and tears, promising healing and extended life?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:5 shows God's mercy as He hears Hezekiah's prayer and sees his tears, responding with healing and added life.

questions.question: What sign did God give Hezekiah through Isaiah to confirm his healing, involving the shadow on the dial of Ahaz?
options: The shadow moving forward ten degrees
The shadow returning backward ten degrees
questions.correctAnswer: The shadow returning backward ten degrees
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 20:10-11, Hezekiah requests the shadow move backward ten degrees, which God miraculously does, confirming the healing promise.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 20:6, why does God promise to protect Jerusalem and Hezekiah from the king of Assyria?
options: For the sake of David and God's own sake
To demonstrate God's power over Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: For the sake of David and God's own sake
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:6 explicitly states God's protection is for His servant David's sake and His own name's sake, revealing God's faithfulness to His covenant.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about prayer and divine hearing is illustrated by Hezekiah's interaction with Isaiah and the LORD?
options: God ignores prayers of the righteous
God hears and responds to sincere prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and responds to sincere prayer
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:3-5 shows that Hezekiah's heartfelt prayer leads God to respond with healing, demonstrating that God hears and acts on sincere prayers.

questions.question: How does Hezekiah's showing of all his treasures to the Babylonian envoys reflect on his understanding of divine wisdom and prudence?
options: It shows his wise political strategy
It reveals a lack of godly wisdom and prudence
It demonstrates his complete trust in God
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals a lack of godly wisdom and prudence
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:13-15 indicates Hezekiah showed all his treasures to envoys, which Isaiah rebukes in 2 Kings 20:16-18 as leading to future judgment, revealing poor prudence.

questions.question: What future judgment does Isaiah prophesy concerning Hezekiah’s descendants and treasures, and what doctrine does this emphasize?
options: Babylon will carry away treasures and sons, emphasizing God's judgment
God will restore all treasures and descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon will carry away treasures and sons, emphasizing God's judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:17-18 prophesy that Babylon will carry away treasures and Hezekiah’s descendants, highlighting the doctrine of divine judgment on disobedience.

questions.question: In what way does Hezekiah’s prayer in 2 Kings 20:3 reveal the theological concept of sanctification or holiness?
options: He acknowledges walking before God in truth and a perfect heart
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledges walking before God in truth and a perfect heart
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's prayer in 2 Kings 20:3 reveals his awareness of living a life pleasing to God, reflecting sanctification as walking in truth and sincerity before the LORD.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God’s sovereignty and covenant faithfulness is taught by 2 Kings 20:5-6 and 2 Kings 20:11?
options: God is limited by human actions
God sovereignly controls nature and extends life according to covenant promises
God’s promises are conditional on human power
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls nature and extends life according to covenant promises
questions.explanation: These verses show God miraculously controlling the shadow and extending Hezekiah’s life, demonstrating God's sovereign power and faithfulness to His covenant (2 Kings 20:5-6,11).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 20:1-3 and 2 Kings 20:19 together emphasize the theological tension between divine judgment and peace?
options: Peace is unrelated to divine judgment
God’s word includes judgment but also offers peace and truth
Peace is only available after death
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word includes judgment but also offers peace and truth
questions.explanation: Hezekiah faces death judgment but prays for mercy (2 Kings 20:1-3), and later accepts God’s word as good if it brings peace and truth in his days (2 Kings 20:19), showing this tension.

questions.question: What narrative role does Hezekiah’s recovery and extended life play in the broader redemptive story of Scripture as seen in 2 Kings 20:6 and 2 Kings 20:21?
options: It signifies the end of God’s covenant with David
It preserves the Davidic line through Manasseh’s succession
It fulfills a promise to Babylonian kings
It demonstrates the failure of prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It preserves the Davidic line through Manasseh’s succession
questions.explanation: God extends Hezekiah’s life to preserve Jerusalem and the Davidic covenant lineage, leading to Manasseh’s reign (2 Kings 20:6,21), crucial for the messianic line in redemptive history.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that miraculous signs like the shadow moving backward could be natural phenomena or legend. What does 2 Kings 20:9-11 teach about this event?
options: It was a natural solar eclipse
It was a divinely orchestrated miracle confirming God’s word
It was a misunderstanding of ancient timekeeping
It was a symbolic story with no historical basis
questions.correctAnswer: It was a divinely orchestrated miracle confirming God’s word
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:9-11 records Isaiah praying and God causing the shadow to move backward ten degrees, affirming the event as a genuine miracle confirming divine authority.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in 2 Kings 20:6 by His promise to defend the city for His own sake and for David's sake?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: The promise to defend Jerusalem for His own and David's sake (2 Kings 20:6) reveals God's faithfulness to His covenant promises, an unchanging divine attribute.

questions.question: What does Hezekiah’s reaction to Isaiah’s prophecy about Babylon’s future captivity reveal about his understanding of God’s sovereignty and peace (2 Kings 20:19)?
options: He rejects God's word as harsh
He accepts God's word as good if it brings peace and truth
He tries to bribe Babylon to avoid captivity
questions.correctAnswer: He accepts God's word as good if it brings peace and truth
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 20:19, Hezekiah calls God's word good, showing submission to divine sovereignty and a desire for peace and truth despite coming judgment.

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s providence over human history is revealed by the narrative of Hezekiah making a pool and conduit in 2 Kings 20:20?
options: God is uninvolved in practical human affairs
God empowers human initiative for city protection
Water management was irrelevant in ancient times
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers human initiative for city protection
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 20:20 shows Hezekiah's preparation for Jerusalem's defense by securing water, illustrating God's providential empowerment of human effort within His sovereign plan.

questions.question: What synthesis of verses 2 Kings 20:12-15 and 2 Kings 20:16-18 teaches about human pride and divine judgment in the context of international relations?
options: Revealing all possessions to foreign powers invites divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Revealing all possessions to foreign powers invites divine judgment
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's pride in showing treasures to Babylon (2 Kings 20:12-15) leads Isaiah to warn of Babylonian exile (2 Kings 20:16-18), teaching divine judgment on arrogant political openness.
